title: ENSO-adjusted autumn DMI skewness had an interval that includes zero in 1950-2024
abstract: We tested autumn Indian Ocean Dipole Mode Index skewness in 75 years from 1950 to 2024. Raw skewness was 0.644, with a 95% five-year block interval of 0.208 to 1.019. After fitting a linear time trend and linear and squared Nino 3.4 terms, residual skewness was 0.641, with a refitted interval of -0.106 to 1.278. Thus adjustment left a positive estimate but uncertain evidence for nonzero residual skewness. One- and three-year blocks gave the same uncertainty conclusion. Later-minus-earlier skewness at a 1987 split was -0.831, with interval -1.857 to 0.823. Omitting 1997 and 2019 left a positive estimate. These results do not show that ENSO removes asymmetry or that the residual distribution is symmetric. The study provides a reproducible distribution benchmark, not a new physical mechanism. Few seasons, revised SST products, simple adjustment and block assumptions limit inference. External source and annual records remain outside the baseline package. Code, source hashes, aggregate evidence, a figure and an independent numerical audit are included.

display.caption: Autumn DMI skewness and 95% percentile intervals from 9,999 paired five-year block samples with model refitting. Linear and quadratic labels include a time trend and ENSO. Period and omission rows use the quadratic model. Zero is a reference, not proof of symmetry.
